title: a11y-ui-src configuration contract
purpose: Generate valid run specs (the workflow files the headless runner takes and other tools exchange) and app configuration files, including custom steps.

runSpec.description: A workflow run as a file: what the headless runner takes (node src/cli/run-workflow.js <spec.json>), what the app opens with Load config, and what the app saves inside every configuration as its "runSpec". The format to generate.
notes: customSteps is an array of custom-step definitions, not a JSON string.

A run has no profile: each a11yScan step's profile sets what it checks against, WCAG 2.2 at a level (wcag22-a, wcag22-aa, wcag22-aaa) or a standard (en301549-v4.1.1, en301549-v3.2.1); without one, wcag22-aa. There is no profile, wcag, tags or globalEvidenceFormat field on a run any more: node src/cli/convert-config.js puts an older run's profile on its scans.

context (Include selectors in the app) limits every scan to the elements its CSS selectors match; exclude (Exclude selectors) leaves those its selectors match out. A scan's own context replaces the run's; its own exclude adds to it.
viewport is a preset name (default, desktop-xlg, desktop-lg, desktop-md, tablet, mobile) or {width, height}.
vars sets starting variables, read by the steps as {var:name}.

The schema is strict: only the fields each step declares, and only the listed values where a field lists them. --check reports a field a step does not declare, or an unlisted value, as a warning, since the runner still runs it.
Check a spec with node src/cli/run-workflow.js <spec.json> --check before running it: exit 0 means it can run, 2 lists every error.
A secret field (setPassword's value) has no way to be supplied to an unattended run yet.
The app opens a run spec with Load config: its vars go into a Batch row, and a viewport size that is not a preset, which the app has no setting for, is reported when it opens.

A secret field (secret: true in the action catalog, the value of setPassword) takes {"$env": "NAME"} in place of the value: whatever runs the workflow reads that environment variable as the run starts, and the run stops before a browser opens when it is not set. Write a reference rather than a password, which a spec must never hold.

batchSpec.description: One workflow run once per row, as the app's Batch section runs it: what to generate for the same workflow over several pages or variants. node src/cli/run-workflow.js <batch.json> runs it.
notes: Each row is { name, url, vars } and nothing else; values the workflow reads go in vars, read as {var:name}.
A row without a url starts on the spec's url; a spec whose every row has a url needs none of its own.
Without a namePattern every row needs a name, and no two runs may share one.
The spec's own vars are every row's; a row's vars win.

configFile.description: What the app's Save configuration writes and Load configuration reads (*.a11y-config.json): the form as the user left it, the run spec it comes to, and the batch rows when there are any.
notes: state[actions-workflow] must be a JSON array of action objects.
custom steps are stored in state[custom-steps-json] as a JSON string that serializes an array of custom-step definitions.
Keep keys stable and human-authored: do not include random UI-generated field IDs.

Secret fields (secret: true in the action catalog, the value of setPassword) are never written to a config: the step carries "<field>Masked": true and no value. Supply the value again in the app before such a config can run; unattended runs cannot recover it. A setValue step with "valueMasked": true, saved before setPassword existed, is loaded as setPassword. A reference ({"$env": "NAME"}) is saved as it is: it holds no secret.
The schema checks state[actions-workflow] against the same step definitions as the run spec, and runSpec as a run spec.
batch holds the Batch section: rows (each { name, url, vars }, no other fields), namePattern and enabled.
--check reports a configuration's own fields too: an unknown field or unlisted value is a warning, except in a batch row, where it is an error because the app will not queue that batch.
actions must be a non-empty array.
customSteps is optional; include it when actions use runCustomStep.

hardRules: A run spec has type=a11y-run-spec, specVersion=1, a url and actions. An app configuration has version=1, type=a11y-ui-src-config and state.
The steps are a run spec's actions, or an app configuration's state.actions-workflow: an array of actions.
Each action object must include a valid type from actionTypeEnum.
If an action type is runCustomStep, customStepId must reference an existing custom step id.
custom step ids must be unique and non-empty.
runCustomStep.argsJson, when provided, must be a JSON object string.
runCustomStep blocks indirect cycles by default and enforces max nesting depth; direct self-recursion is allowed only when allowRecursion=true.
Missing required custom step inputs cause runtime errors.
runCustomStep on a custom step with an empty actions array is a no-op (it does not throw).

Fields of type "number" accept a literal number or a single variable token such as "{var:count}". The variable is turned into a number when the step runs; fields marked integer need a whole number. A value that is not a number is ignored (the field falls back to its default) and a warning is logged.

compatibility.whenLoadedInOldAppWithoutCustomSteps: custom-steps fields are ignored and runCustomStep actions are unknown/omitted or fail; custom-step behavior is lost.
compatibility.guidance: For backward compatibility, avoid runCustomStep and inline actions directly in actions-workflow.

generationChecklist: Emit valid JSON with no comments or trailing commas.
Write a run spec (outputFormats.runSpec): the runner takes it and the app opens it. A configuration file (outputFormats.configFile) is what the app saves; there is no need to write one.
Run spec: include type, specVersion, url and actions; custom steps go in customSteps as an array.
Configuration file: include version, type, url (optional), state, metadata.createdAt (recommended); always include state.actions-workflow as an array, and custom steps in state.custom-steps-json.
Use only action types listed in actionTypeEnum.
When using custom steps, keep runCustomStep's customStepId and the custom step ids in sync.
Do not invent undocumented fields unless explicitly allowed by the action definition.
Prefer stable, minimal state keys; avoid random UI control IDs.
Check the result with node src/cli/run-workflow.js <file> --check and fix every error it reports.

a11yScan.label: A11y scan
a11yScan.description: Run an accessibility scan on the current page or within a selector. You can narrow the scan to a region using 'context' and exclude noisy areas using 'exclude'.

label.label: Scan label
label.description: Label shown in reports and live stream. Supports {var:name}, {index}, {oneBased}, {total}.

scanTags.label: Tags
scanTags.description: Free-form tags for this scan. Used to filter the report by tag once the run finishes. Supports {var:name}, {index}, {oneBased}, {total}, so a single tag like {var:viewport} fills in per iteration. Pick tags already used elsewhere in this workflow or add new ones.

profile.label: Profile
profile.description: The profile this scan checks against, WCAG 2.2 AA unless it says otherwise: WCAG 2.2 at Level A, AA or AAA, or a standard, which sets the WCAG version and the level, all of them Level A and AA: EN 301 549 V4.1.1, the EU standard, which is WCAG 2.2, and EN 301 549 V3.2.1, its earlier version, which is WCAG 2.1 and still checks 4.1.1 Parsing. surea11y applies a standard in full, version details such as 4.1.1 included. Including rule IDs or tags explicitly takes precedence over a standard. Passing the rules does not mean the page meets the standard: many criteria still need a manual check.

context.label: Include selectors
context.description: The parts of the page this scan checks: every element these CSS selectors match, comma separated. Empty, the scan checks the whole page. A selector that matches nothing scans nothing, and the report says so.

exclude.label: Exclude selectors
exclude.description: The parts of the page this scan leaves out: every element these CSS selectors match, comma separated.

includeBestPractice.label: Include best-practice rules
includeBestPractice.description: Also run the best-practice rules in this scan: good practice beyond the profile, such as landmarks and heading order. The profile alone never runs them. Their findings are listed in a Best practices section of their own and count toward no criterion, score, compliance rate or comparison.

locale.label: Results language
locale.description: Language surea11y writes its findings in: rule titles, what failed, how to fix it, and the WCAG criteria names. Rules that judge wording, such as vague link text or generic headings, go by the language of the page, not this setting.

applyDefaultStyle.label: Blur exclusions
applyDefaultStyle.description: Blur and fade the parts of the page the scan leaves out (Exclude selectors, and what is outside Context) in the scan's screenshots, so they show what was checked.

preserveHover.label: Preserve hover state
preserveHover.description: Keep current :hover styling for this scan/evidence capture. Disable to clear transient hover before capture.

waitTimeout.label: Wait timeout (ms)
waitTimeout.description: How long Wait for waits for its selector before the step fails.

stageTimeout.label: Time limit per stage (ms)
stageTimeout.description: The most each stage of the scan may take before it is given up on: loading the engine into the page, letting the page settle, the page ready wait, the check itself and the screenshot. Pictures of flagged elements get their own time on top.

pageReadyTimeout.label: Page ready timeout (ms)
pageReadyTimeout.description: Before scanning, wait up to this long for the page to finish loading: the load event, web fonts and images (not lazy ones). If it has not finished by then, the scan runs anyway and its report says what was still loading. 0 checks without waiting.

heavyNodeThreshold.label: Skip pages with more elements than
heavyNodeThreshold.description: Skip this scan when the page has more elements than this, rather than wait on a very slow scan. The report says the scan was skipped, and why.

waitForSelector.label: Wait for
waitForSelector.description: Start the scan only once this selector is on the page, for content that loads late. If it does not appear within the wait timeout, the step fails rather than scanning the page without it.

waitVisible.label: Require visibility
waitVisible.description: With Wait for, wait until the element is visible, not only on the page.

includeRuleIds.label: Include rules
includeRuleIds.description: The only rules this scan runs: the rest of its level's rules do not. Name a WCAG criterion (wcag-1.4.3-contrast-minimum) to check it in full, or single checks (contrast-minimum); a criterion only some of whose checks run is reported as partly checked unless one of them fails. Use a comma separated string.

excludeRuleIds.label: Exclude rules
excludeRuleIds.description: Rule IDs to exclude for this scan only. Use a comma separated string.

includeTags.label: Include tags
includeTags.description: Run only the rules with these tags, within the scan's WCAG version and level (rules that test no WCAG criterion, such as best practices, as tagged). Their criteria are reported as with Include rules: partly checked when some of a criterion's checks do not run. Use a comma separated string.

excludeTags.label: Exclude tags
excludeTags.description: Rule tags to exclude for this scan only. Use a comma separated string.

includeMode.label: Combine Include rules and tags
includeMode.description: With both Include rules and Include tags: run only the rules that are in both, or every rule that is in either.

engineMode.label: Checking mode
engineMode.description: Auditor support makes the assumptions an auditor would where the page leaves something unset, such as a white background behind the page; Strict conformance assumes nothing the page does not state.

findingsSource.label: Report findings by
findingsSource.description: Whether findings are reported per WCAG success criterion, gathering the checks behind each one, or per single check, or both.

screenshotView.label: Screenshot view
screenshotView.description: Take a screenshot of the page once the scan is done, shown with its results. Set to false for a scan that needs no picture of the page: it runs faster and its report is smaller. Pictures of the flagged elements (Element screenshots) are set apart.

elementScreenshots.label: Element screenshots
elementScreenshots.description: Take a picture of each element surea11y flags, with a box around it, shown beside its finding. A finding that shows only with the WCAG text spacing applied also gets a picture with the spacing applied, beside the one of the page as it is.

elementScreenshotsMax.label: Most element screenshots
elementScreenshotsMax.description: The most pictures one scan takes when Element screenshots is on; 0 for no limit, though a scan still has 30 seconds for its pictures. Elements past it say so beside their finding.

elementScreenshotsPerRule.label: Most element screenshots per rule
elementScreenshotsPerRule.description: The most elements pictured for each rule, so the rules checked first don't take every picture; 0 for no limit. An element pictured for one rule shows that picture under every rule that flags it.

click.label: Click
click.description: Click by selector, or click by visible text (labelText). When labelText is set, selector becomes an optional scope.

selector.label: Element selector / scope selector
selector.description: If labelText is NOT set, this is the CSS selector for the element to click. If labelText IS set, this is an optional scope container selector. Use :ctx inside forEachElement.

labelText.label: Text to click
labelText.description: Visible text (or accessible name sources) to find. If set, this is the target, and selector is treated as an optional scope.

programmatic.label: Programmatic click
programmatic.description: Click by calling the element's click() in the page, instead of with the mouse: for an element the mouse cannot reach, such as one something else covers.

mouseButton.label: Mouse button
mouseButton.description: If the click is done with the left or right button.

clickKind.label: Single or double click
clickKind.description: If it is single or double click.

scrollIntoView.label: Scroll into view
scrollIntoView.description: Scroll the element to the center of the viewport before clicking. A pointer click may still scroll if the element is outside the viewport.

caseSensitive.label: Case sensitive (labelText)
caseSensitive.description: Use case-sensitive comparison when clicking by labelText.

exact.label: Exact match (labelText)
exact.description: Match full text when true. Default is substring match.

allowPointerFallback.label: Allow pointer fallback
allowPointerFallback.description: When clicking by labelText, allow clicking non-interactive targets near the matched text.

pointerFallbackMaxMatches.label: Pick nth match
pointerFallbackMaxMatches.description: When labelText appears multiple times, pick the nth visible match (1 = first).

timeout.label: Timeout (ms)
timeout.description: When clicking by labelText, how long to wait for the target to appear.

waitUntil.label: Wait until
waitUntil.description: If set, waits for a possible navigation after the click.

retries.label: Retry attempts
retries.description: Extra attempts if the click fails.

optional.label: Optional action
optional.description: Do not stop the workflow if this click fails.

setColorScheme.label: Set color scheme and contrast
setColorScheme.description: Show the page in the light or dark color scheme, in high contrast, or both, as a browser or system set to them would. The color scheme sets prefers-color-scheme, which the page's media queries follow; until a step sets it, the page is shown as the run's configuration says (the browser's default, light, unless it says otherwise), and Run default goes back to that. High contrast shows the page in forced colors, as Windows' contrast themes do: the browser replaces the page's colors with the user's, and its forced-colors media queries and system colors such as Canvas and GrayText follow, so a scan or a screenshot shows what stays visible then (focus indicators, icons, borders of controls). Leave either one empty to keep it as it is. Both stay until another step changes them, across navigation. A site with its own theme switch that does not follow prefers-color-scheme needs a click on that switch instead. surea11y still measures contrast in the page's own colors in high contrast, as WCAG asks, and each scan says it was taken in it. High contrast needs Chrome.

colorScheme.label: Color scheme
colorScheme.description: The color scheme to switch to, or Run default for the one the run started with (its configuration's, the browser's own unless it sets one). Empty keeps the current one.

highContrast.label: High contrast
highContrast.description: Show the page in forced colors (high contrast), or stop, or Run default for what the run started with (its configuration's, Off unless it says otherwise). Empty keeps it as it is.

optional.label: Optional action

setLanguage.label: Set language
setLanguage.description: Show the page in a language, as a browser set to it would: the Accept-Language header a server picks a language by, navigator.language and navigator.languages for a site that picks it in its scripts, and the format of dates and numbers. It stays set until another Set language step changes it, across navigation, refreshes and pages the workflow opens. The open page loads again so it shows the new language now; a page that has not loaded yet picks it up when it does. Run default goes back to the language the run started with: its configuration's, or the browser's own when it sets none. Each scan says the language it was taken in, and warns when the page declares another (its html lang): a site that keeps its language in a cookie, an account setting or its address (such as /en/), or picks it by location, may not follow this step. Dates and numbers need Chrome.

language.label: Language

customLanguage.label: Other language
customLanguage.description: A language not in the list, as a BCP 47 tag (es-MX, fr-CA, zh-Hant-HK, a variable such as {var:lang}). Used instead of Language when filled.

reload.label: Reload the page
reload.description: Load the open page again, so it shows the new language now. Off, it shows it from the next page loaded.

mergedScan.label: Merged scan
mergedScan.description: Report the A11y scans inside it as one scan: the same view scanned in several contexts (light and dark theme, desktop and mobile width) counts once. Each scan inside is a context, named by its label; a failure lists the contexts it occurs in, and one whose result differs between contexts (a different contrast ratio, a different size) is listed once per result. The merged scan holds every context's screenshot. Variables set inside stay available after it. A Merged scan cannot contain another.

label.label: Scan name
label.description: The merged scan's name in the report. {var:...} tokens work, so a Repeat over pages can name each one. Without it, the first context's name is used.

scanTags.label: Tags
scanTags.description: The merged scan's tags, used to filter the report by tag and to break the live totals down. The tags of the scans inside describe their contexts and are shown with them; when this is empty, the merged scan takes all of theirs. Supports {var:name}, {index}, {oneBased}, {total}.

actions.label: Actions
actions.description: The steps to run, with an A11y scan for each context. A scan with no label is named by its place, as "Scan 2 of 4".

examples.title: One scan of a page in light and dark

runCustomStep.label: Custom step
runCustomStep.description: Run a reusable custom step by id. Inputs are provided as a JSON object and become scoped variables for nested actions. For repeated calls that only differ by input values, prefer one runCustomStep inside a repeat dataset.

customStepId.label: Custom step name
customStepId.description: Name of the custom step definition to run.

argsJson.label: Inputs (JSON object)
argsJson.description: Optional inputs passed to this custom step: an object, or the same object as JSON text. Example: {"label":"Settings"}

exportVars.label: Export vars
exportVars.description: Optional variable names to copy back to parent scope after execution.

maxDepth.label: Max nesting depth
maxDepth.description: Safety limit for nested custom step calls.

allowRecursion.label: Allow direct self-recursion
allowRecursion.description: Allow only direct self-recursion for this call (A -> A). Indirect cycles (A -> B -> A) are still blocked.

optional.label: Optional step
optional.description: If true and this call fails, mark as failed-optional and continue.

if.label: Condition
if.description: Run one branch when the condition is true, otherwise run elseActions. Variables set inside a branch (getText, getCount, setVar) are only available to later steps in that branch; to use a value after the condition, set it before or outside it.

selectorExists.label: Selector exists
selectorExists.description: Condition is true if this selector exists. Use :ctx inside forEachElement.

urlIncludes.label: URL includes
urlIncludes.description: Condition is true if the URL includes this substring.

actions.label: If actions
actions.description: Actions to run when the condition is true.

elseActions.label: Else actions
elseActions.description: Actions to run when the condition is false.

onlyVisible.label: Only visible items
onlyVisible.description: When true, only iterate elements that are visible (non-zero size, not display:none, not visibility:hidden).

equals.label: Equals value
equals.description: Value to compare against the variable, as text: 2310 matches a variable holding the number 2310, and true matches true.

optional.label: Optional block
optional.description: If true and the block fails, mark as failed-optional and continue.

examples.title: Apply promo code if field exists

ifUrl.label: URL condition
ifUrl.description: Compare one part of the current page URL (domain name, port, path, query string, one query parameter or fragment) with a value, and run one branch when the comparison is true, otherwise run elseActions. Variables set inside a branch are only available to later steps in that branch.

urlPart.label: URL part
urlPart.description: Which part of the URL to compare. For https://shop.example.com:8443/cart/checkout?step=2&lang=en#payment: domain name is shop.example.com, port is 8443 (a URL with no port uses the protocol's default, 443 for https and 80 for http), path is /cart/checkout, query string is step=2&lang=en, the query parameter "step" is 2, and fragment is payment.

paramName.label: Parameter name
paramName.description: Name of the query parameter to compare, when URL part is "One query parameter". A parameter missing from the URL equals nothing and contains nothing, so "is different from" and "does not contain" are true for it.

comparison.label: Comparison
comparison.description: How to compare the URL part with the value.

value.label: Value
value.description: Text to compare with, without the leading ? or # (either is ignored if typed). Empty means the part is empty: a fragment equal to nothing means the URL has no fragment. The domain name is compared ignoring case; every other part is case-sensitive. Supports {var:name}.

actions.label: If actions
actions.description: Actions to run when the comparison is true.

elseActions.label: Else actions
elseActions.description: Actions to run when the comparison is false.

optional.label: Optional block
optional.description: If true and the block fails, mark as failed-optional and continue.

examples.title: Go back to the site if a link left the domain

switch.label: Switch
switch.description: Compare one value, a part of the current page URL or a variable, with each case in order, and run the first case that matches; when none matches, run the default actions. Variables set inside a case are only available to later steps in that case.

subject.label: Compare
subject.description: What the cases are compared with: a part of the current page URL, or a workflow variable.

options.label: A part of the page URL

urlPart.label: URL part
urlPart.description: When comparing a part of the URL: which part. Read like the URL condition step: no leading ? or #, and a URL with no port is on its protocol's default one.

paramName.label: Parameter name
paramName.description: When the URL part is "One query parameter": the parameter's name.

var.label: Variable name
var.description: When comparing a variable: its name. Found the way {var:name} finds it; an unset variable equals nothing and contains nothing.

cases.label: Cases
cases.description: The cases, checked in order. The first one that matches runs, and the rest are not checked.

defaultActions.label: Default actions
defaultActions.description: Actions to run when no case matches.

optional.label: Optional block
optional.description: If true and the block fails, mark as failed-optional and continue.

examples.title: Different actions per component examples page

case.label: Case
case.description: One case of a switch: when the switch's value matches, its actions run. Only used inside a switch's cases.

comparison.label: Comparison
comparison.description: How to compare the switch's value with this case's value.

value.label: Value
value.description: Text to compare with. For a URL part, compared the way the URL condition step compares it. Supports {var:name}.

actions.label: Case actions
actions.description: Actions to run when this case matches.

repeat.label: Repeat
repeat.description: Run the same list of actions multiple times, either by a fixed repetition count or by iterating over a dataset (one item per line). Useful for replacing duplicated actions that only differ by one value.

repetitions.label: Repetitions
repetitions.description: How many times to repeat. Accepts a whole number or a variable token such as {var:count} (for example, a count stored by "Count elements into variable"). The variable is turned into a number when the step runs; if it is not a whole number the repeat runs 0 times and a warning is logged.

itemsText.label: Dataset (one item per line)
itemsText.description: Optional dataset to drive iterations. Each non-empty line is one item. Lines may be plain text (mapped to item.value and available as {var:value}) or JSON objects (mapped to item.key and available as {var:item.key}). All values are normalized to strings. When provided, this overrides repetitions. Use this with runCustomStep argsJson to avoid repeating the same custom-step call for each static value.

continueOnIterationError.label: Continue on error
continueOnIterationError.description: If an iteration fails, the process continues to the next iteration.

optional.label: Optional block
optional.description: If one iteration fails, mark as failed-optional and continue.

closeWorkerPages.label: Close worker pages
closeWorkerPages.description: Whether to close worker pages after all repeat iterations complete.

maxSeconds.label: Max time (s)
maxSeconds.description: Maximum allowed execution time (in seconds) for the entire repeat action.

perPageDelayMs.label: Delay per page (ms)
perPageDelayMs.description: Optional delay (in milliseconds) applied between iteration executions.

examples.title: Iterate viewport presets for one custom-step call

forEachElement.label: Iterate
forEachElement.description: Repeat actions for each element that matches a selector. Inside, use :ctx to target the current element. Use {index}, {oneBased}, and {total} in strings. This is for DOM elements; use repeat for static value lists.

targetSelector.label: Items selector
targetSelector.description: Selector that returns one or many elements.

onlyVisible.label: Only visible items
onlyVisible.description: When true, only iterate elements that are visible (non-zero size, not display:none, not visibility:hidden).

concurrency.label: Concurrency
concurrency.description: Number of concurrent workers used to process iterations, from 1 to 8. When greater than 1, each iteration runs in its own isolated worker page.

continueOnIterationError.label: Continue on error
continueOnIterationError.description: If an iteration fails, the process continues to the next iteration.

maxIterationErrors.label: Max iteration errors
maxIterationErrors.description: If set, stop after this many iteration errors (only applies when 'Continue on error' is enabled).

iterSetupActions.label: Iteration setup
iterSetupActions.description: Actions that run before collecting items, and again before each iteration. Use this to reveal menus or panels that contain the target elements. Do not use :ctx here.

preActions.label: Pre-actions
preActions.description: Actions that run after an item is selected and scoped, before the main actions. Use :ctx here.

actions.label: Actions
actions.description: Actions to run on each item. Use :ctx to target the current item.

limit.label: Max items
limit.description: Max number of elements to process. 0 means unlimited.

reverse.label: Reverse order
reverse.description: Iterate from last to first when true.

isolation.label: Isolation
isolation.description: With a concurrency above 1, whether the extra pages share cookies and session with the main page (page), or each runs in a browser context of its own (context).

closeWorkerPages.label: Close worker pages
closeWorkerPages.description: Close the extra pages a concurrency above 1 opened once every item is done.

maxSeconds.label: Max time (s)
maxSeconds.description: Maximum allowed execution time (in seconds) for the entire repeat action.

perPageDelayMs.label: Delay per iteration (ms)
perPageDelayMs.description: Optional delay (in milliseconds) applied between iteration executions.

dynamic.label: Dynamic selection
dynamic.description: Re-evaluate the selector on each iteration. Use this when the DOM list changes between iterations.

examples.title: Hover to reveal a panel, then iterate links

crawlQueue.label: Crawl queue
crawlQueue.description: Depth-limited crawl with strict budgets. For each visited page, run nested actions, then discover and enqueue new links.

maxDepth.label: Max depth
maxDepth.description: Maximum link depth to follow from seeds. 0 means only the seed pages.

strategy.label: Strategy
strategy.description: Queue strategy: 'By level first' or 'Deep as possible first'.

isolation.label: Isolation
isolation.description: Whether worker pages share cookies and session with the main page (page), or run in isolated browser contexts (context).

maxPages.label: Max pages
maxPages.description: Maximum number of pages to visit.

continueOnIterationError.label: Continue on error
continueOnIterationError.description: If an iteration fails, the process continues to the next iteration.

actions.label: Actions for each visited page
actions.description: Actions to run on every visited page, typically navigate + a11yScan.

sameOriginOnly.label: Same origin only
sameOriginOnly.description: Only crawl URLs on the same origin as the seed/current page.

maxLinksPerPage.label: Max links per page
maxLinksPerPage.description: Maximum number of discovered links to enqueue per visited page.

include.label: Include patterns
include.description: One pattern per line. Supports /regex/flags or wildcards (* and ?). If set, only matching URLs are enqueued.

exclude.label: Exclude patterns
exclude.description: One pattern per line. Supports /regex/flags or wildcards (* and ?). Matching URLs are skipped.

queueVar.label: Queue variable
queueVar.description: Variable path storing the URL queue (array).

varNs.label: Variable namespace
varNs.description: Namespace used for per-page variables: crawl_url, crawl_depth, crawl_index, crawl_total.

skipIteration.label: Skip iteration
skipIteration.description: Inside a loop (For each element, Repeat or Crawl), skip the rest of the current item when its conditions match, and go on with the next one. Each field you fill in is one condition: Selector exists; each check on the element of Element selector (Text equals, Text contains, Attribute equals, Attribute contains, or Attribute name alone for having it); URL includes; Variable equals. The item is skipped when all of them match, or, with Use OR, when any of them does. A step with no condition never skips. Text checks are case-sensitive and read the text with its spaces collapsed. In a Crawl, a skipped page's links are not followed.

selector.label: Element selector
selector.description: The element the text and attribute checks read: the first one this selector matches. Use :ctx for the current item (:ctx alone for the item itself). If nothing matches, each of those checks fails. On its own, with no check, the element being there is the condition.

selectorExists.label: Selector exists
selectorExists.description: A condition: an element matches this selector. Use :ctx for inside the current item. Independent of Element selector.

selectorAttr.label: Attribute name
selectorAttr.description: The element's attribute that Attribute equals and Attribute contains read. With neither, the condition is that the element has it.

attrEquals.label: Attribute equals
attrEquals.description: A condition: the attribute's value is exactly this.

attrContains.label: Attribute contains
attrContains.description: A condition: the attribute's value contains this.

selectorTextEquals.label: Text equals
selectorTextEquals.description: A condition: the element's text is exactly this.

selectorTextContains.label: Text contains
selectorTextContains.description: A condition: the element's text contains this.

varEquals.label: Variable equals
varEquals.description: A condition: the variable equals this, compared as text (2310 equals the number 2310). An unset variable equals nothing.

urlIncludes.label: URL includes
urlIncludes.description: A condition: the page's address contains this.

or.label: Use OR across conditions
or.description: Skip when any condition matches, instead of only when all of them do.

examples.title: Skip links to other sites that offer a download (both must match)
Skip sold-out items, or anything on an archive page (either is enough)

goBack.label: Go back
goBack.description: Navigate back in history and wait until the page is ready.

optional.label: Optional action
optional.description: Do not stop the workflow if this action fails.

screenshot.label: Screenshot
screenshot.description: Capture a screenshot at the current state and attach it to the results.

label.label: Display label
label.description: Display label for logs and reports.

optional.label: Optional action
optional.description: Do not stop the workflow if this action fails.

preserveHover.label: Preserve hover state
preserveHover.description: Keep current :hover styling in this screenshot. Disable to clear transient hover before capture.

getText.label: Get text into variable
getText.description: Read textContent from the first matching element and store it into a variable.

var.label: Variable name
var.description: Variable name to store the value.

attr.label: Attribute name
attr.description: If set, reads the given attribute instead of textContent (e.g. href, aria-label, data-id).

rawAttr.label: Read raw attribute value
rawAttr.description: When attr is href, read the raw HTML attribute (e.g. ../page.html) instead of the resolved absolute URL.

useInnerText.label: Use rendered text (innerText)
useInnerText.description: Use innerText instead of textContent. Slower but respects visibility and CSS.

trim.label: Trim whitespace
trim.description: Trim and collapse whitespace when true.

getCount.label: Count elements into variable
getCount.description: Count the elements that match a selector (including inside open shadow roots) and store the number into a variable. Stores 0 when nothing matches. The variable can be used in number fields, e.g. repeat's repetitions: {var:count}.

var.label: Variable name
var.description: Variable name to store the count.

logValue.label: Log the value
logValue.description: Write the stored count to the run log.

setVar.label: Set variable
setVar.description: Set a workflow variable to a literal value. Strings support {var:name} expansion.

value.label: Value
value.description: Value to assign. For strings, you can use {var:name}.

from.label: Source
from.description: Set from a runtime source instead of a literal value. Supported: url.

clearVar.label: Clear variable
clearVar.description: Remove a variable from the workflow variable map.

collectOutput.label: Collect metadata
collectOutput.description: Record a value into the run's collected-metadata report, grouped by key. Useful inside loops (forEachElement/repeat/crawlQueue) to build a list of values across pages, optionally only when a condition holds.

key.label: Key
key.description: Grouping key for the report panel. Supports {var:name}.

value.label: Literal value
value.description: Literal/template value to record. Supports {var:name}, {index}, {oneBased}, {total}. Exactly one of value/fromVar/from must be set.

fromVar.label: From variable
fromVar.description: Record the current value of this workflow variable.

from.label: From page
from.description: Record a page-derived value instead of a literal/variable.

label.label: Display label
label.description: Display label; defaults to the key.

selector.label: Element selector
selector.description: Used when from is selectorText or selectorAttr. Use selector: "title" for the page title, "h1" for the main heading.

attr.label: Attribute name
attr.description: Used when from is selectorAttr (e.g. href, aria-label).

trim.label: Trim whitespace
trim.description: Trim and collapse whitespace when reading from the page.

tags.label: Tags
tags.description: Freeform tags rolled up into the report's summary counts (e.g. ["emptyView"]).

when.label: Condition (JSON object)
when.description: Only record when this predicate matches. JSON object with the same shape as skipIteration's condition fields (selectorExists, selector+selectorTextEquals/selectorTextContains, selector+selectorAttr+attrEquals/attrContains, urlIncludes, var+varEquals, or). Omit to always record. Example: {"selectorExists":".empty-state"}

optional.label: Optional action
optional.description: Do not stop the workflow if this action fails.

Save URL only when a view has no data
Log a fixed marker with iteration context

evidenceCapture.label: Save evidence
evidenceCapture.description: Capture a stable page state and attach it as an ordered artifact in the timeline. By default it saves a PNG preview and an MHTML snapshot (includes CSS and assets).

label.label: Display label
label.description: Optional label for the artifact shown in reports and live stream. Supports {var:name}, {index}, {oneBased}, {total}. If empty, the system will generate “Evidence N”.

evidenceVariant.label: Variants to save
evidenceVariant.description: Which variants to generate for this evidence capture.

onError.label: On error
onError.description: What to do if saving evidence fails. Default is to continue the workflow and record the artifact error.

preserveHover.label: Preserve hover state
preserveHover.description: Keep current :hover styling for evidence capture. Disable to clear transient hover before capture.

injectCss.label: Inject CSS
injectCss.description: Inject a CSS <style> tag into the current page. Useful to tweak visuals or stabilize UI behavior (for example, disable animations).

optional.label: Optional action
optional.description: Do not stop the workflow if this action fails.
